note.p: William Adamson of Dublin was proposed for the Society for Constitutional Information (SCI) by John Farnell Tuffin on 2 November 1792 and seconded by William Tooke. In 1773, William Adamson of the Carpenters Company in Dublin voted for Redmond Morres as MP for Dublin City. He subscribed to Reverand Henry Murray of Dublin’s “Evidences of the Jewish and Christian revelations” in 1790. He was also an Irish subscriber to Olaudah Equiano 1793. He was also mentioned in the Methodist “Minutes of some late conversations” on 30 July 1785, the minister of Gospel at North Shields’ “Eight Discourses” on 8 April 1789, and William Myles 1799 notes described him as having been a preacher since 1783 but had departed from the work.
